finding.description: SQL injection vulnerability via unsanitized string concatenation in get_user_by_name.
finding.rationale: User-supplied 'name' is concatenated directly into the SQL query without parameterization or escaping, allowing an attacker to manipulate the query structure and access or modify arbitrary data.

finding.description: SQL injection vulnerability via unsanitized f-string interpolation in get_users_by_ids.
finding.rationale: Each user_id from the comma-split request parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL query without parameterization, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL through the 'ids' query parameter.

finding.description: N+1 query pattern: `get_users_by_ids` issues one separate SQL query per user ID in a loop instead of a single batched query.
finding.rationale: Each iteration executes a round-trip to the database, so fetching N users costs N queries; a single `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (...)` would reduce this to one query regardless of input size.

dependency_reason: Fixing the SQL injection (switching to parameterized queries) and fixing the N+1 pattern (batching into one query) both rewrite get_users_by_ids, so the security fix should be done first to avoid rewriting the same function twice.
